entries.body: Man's chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him forever.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the chief end of man?

entries.body: The word of God, which is contained in the Scriptures of the Old and new Testament, is the only rule to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him.
entries.prompt: WHAT rule has God given to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him?

entries.body: The scriptures principally teach what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.
entries.prompt: WHAT do the scriptures principally teach?

entries.body: God is a Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.
entries.prompt: WHAT is God?

entries.body: There is but one only, the living and true God.
entries.prompt: ARE there more gods than one?

entries.body: There are three persons in the godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.
entries.prompt: HOW many persons are there in the godhead?

entries.body: The decrees of God are his eternal purpose, according to the council of his will, whereby for his own glory he has fore-ordained whatever comes to pass.
entries.prompt: WHAT are the decrees of God?

entries.body: God executes his decrees in the works of creation and providence.
entries.prompt: HOW does God execute his decrees?

entries.body: The work of creation is, God's making all things of nothing, by the word of his power, in the space of six days, and all very good.
entries.prompt: WHAT are the works of creation?

entries.body: God created man male and female, after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness, with doninion over the creatures.
entries.prompt: HOW did God create man?

entries.body: God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures, and all their actions.
entries.prompt: WHAT are God's works of providence?

entries.body: When God created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of perfect obedience, forbidding him to eat of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.
entries.prompt: WHAT special act of providence did God exercise towards man, in the estate wherein he was created?

entries.body: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, fell from the estate wherein they were created, by sinning against God.
entries.prompt: DID our first parents continue in the estate wherein they were created?

entries.body: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of the law of God.
entries.prompt: WHAT is sin?

entries.body: The sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created, was their eating the forbidden fruit.
entries.prompt: WHAT was the sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created?

entries.body: The covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself, but for his posterity, all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in his first transgression.
entries.prompt: DID all mankind fall in Adam's first transgression?

entries.body: The fall brought mankind into a state of sin and misery.
entries.prompt: INTO what estate did the fall bring mankind?

entries.body: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consists in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin, together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.
entries.prompt: WHEREIN consists the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?

entries.body: All mankind by their Jail lost communion with God, are under his wrath and curse; and so made liable to all the miseries in this life, to death itself, and to the pains of Hell forever.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the misery of that estate whereinto man fell?

entries.body: God having out of his mere good pleasure, from all eternity, elected some to everlasting life, did enter into a covenant of grace, to deliver them out of the estate of sin and misery; and to bring them into an estate of salvation by a Redeemer.
entries.prompt: DID God leave all mankind to perish in the estate of sin and misery?

entries.body: The only Redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so teas, and continues to be God and man, in two distinct natures, and one person forever.
entries.prompt: WHO is the Redeemer of God's elect?

entries.body: Christ the Son of God became man by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without sin.
entries.prompt: HOW did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?

entries.body: Christ, as our Redeemer, does execute the office of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his estate of humiliation and exaltation.
entries.prompt: WHAT offices does Christ execute as our Redeemer?

entries.body: Christ executes the office of a prophet, in revealing to us by his word and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.
entries.prompt: HOW does Christ execute the office of a prophet?

entries.body: Christ executes the office of a priest, in his once offering up of himself a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice, and reconcile us to God, and in making continual intercession for us.
entries.prompt: HOW does Christ execute the office of a priest?

entries.body: Christ executes the office of a king, in subduing us to himself, in ruling and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our enemies.
entries.prompt: HOW does Christ execute the office of a king?

entries.body: Christ's humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low condition, made under the law, undergoing the miseries of this life' the wrath of God, and the cursed death of the cross; in being buried, and continuing under the power of death for a time.
entries.prompt: WHEREIN did Christ's humiliation consist?

entries.body: Christ's exaltation consists in his rising again from the dead on the third day; in ascending up into Heaven, in sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.
entries.prompt: WHEREIN consists Christ's exaltation?

entries.body: We are made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.
entries.prompt: HOW are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?

entries.body: By working faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.
entries.prompt: HOW does the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?

entries.body: Effectual calling is the work of God's Spirit, whereby convincing us of our sin and misery, enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our wills, he does persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ, freely offered to us in the gospel.
entries.prompt: WHAT is effectual calling?

entries.body: They that are effectually called do in this life partake of justification, adoption, and sanctification, and the several benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from them.
entries.prompt: WHAT benefits do they that are effectually called partake of in this life?

entries.body: Justification is an act of God's free grace, wherein he pardons all our sins, and accepts us as righteous in his sight, only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.
entries.prompt: WHAT is justification?

entries.body: Adoption is an act of God's free grace, whereby we are received into the number, and have a right to all the privileges of the sons of God.
entries.prompt: WHAT is adoption?

entries.body: Sanctification is the work of God's free grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto sin, and live unto righteousness.
entries.prompt: WHAT is sanctification?

entries.body: The benefits which in this life do either accompany, or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification, are assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance therein to the end.
entries.prompt: WHAT are the benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification?

entries.body: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory; and their bodies being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves until the resurrection.
entries.prompt: WHAT benefits do believers receive from Christ at their death?

entries.body: At the resurrection believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoyment of God to all eternity.
entries.prompt: WHAT benefit do believers receive from Christ at the resurrection?

entries.body: The duty which God requires of man is obedience to his revealed will.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the duty that God requires of man?

entries.body: The rule which God at first revealed to man for his obedience, was the moral law.
entries.prompt: WHAT did God at first reveal to man for the rule of his obedience?

entries.body: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the ten commandments.
entries.prompt: Wherein is the moral law summarily comprehended?

entries.body: The sum of the ten commandments is to love the Lord our God with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our strength, and with all our mind, and our neighbor as ourselves.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the sum of the ten commandments?

entries.body: The preface to the ten commandments is in these words, I am the Lord your God, which have brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the preface to the ten commandments?

entries.body: The first commandment is, You shall have no other gods before me.
entries.prompt: WHICH is the first commandment?

entries.body: The second commandment is, [You shall not make unto you any graven image, or any likeness of anything, that is in Heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth; you shall not bow down yourself to them, nor serve them: For I the Lord your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquities of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the second commandment?

entries.body: The second commandment requires, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious worship and ordinances, as God has appointed in his word.
entries.prompt: What is required in the second commandment?

entries.body: The second commandment forbids the worshiping of God by images, or any other way not appointed in his word.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the second commandment?

entries.body: The reasons annexed to the second commandment, are God's sovereignty over us, his propriety in us, and the zeal he has to his own worship.
entries.prompt: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment?

entries.body: The third commandment is, [You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless, that takes his name in vain.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the third commandment?

entries.body: The third commandment requires the holy and reverend use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, words, and works.
entries.prompt: What is required in the third commandment?

entries.body: The third commandment forbids all profaning or abusing of anything whereby God makes himself known.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the third commandment?

entries.body: The reason annexed to the third commandment is, that however the breakers of this commandment may escape punishment from men, yet the Lord our God will not allow them to escape his righteous judgment.
entries.prompt: What is the reason annexed to the third commandment?

entries.body: The fourth commandment is, [Remember the Sabbath-day, to keep it holy. Six days shall you labor and do all your work; but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God; in it you shall not do any work, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your man-servant, nor your maid-servant, nor your cattle, nor the stranger which is within your gates. For in six days the Lord made Heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day, wherefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath-day, and hallowed it.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the fourth commandment?

entries.body: The fourth commandment requires the keeping holy to God, such set time as he has appointed hi his word, expressly one whole day in seven, to be a holy Sabbath unto the Lord.
entries.prompt: What is required in the fourth commandment?

entries.body: From the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, God appointed the seventh day of the week to be the weekly Sabbath; and the first day of the week ever since, to continue to the end of the world, which is the Christian Sabbath.
entries.prompt: Which day of the seven has God appointed to be the weekly Sabbath?

entries.body: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days, and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God's worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.
entries.prompt: HOW is the Sabbath to be sanctified?

entries.body: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment are, God's allowing us six days of the week for our own employment, his challenging a special propriety in the seventh, his own example, and his blessing the Sabbath-day.
entries.prompt: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment?

entries.body: The fifth commandment is, [Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the fifth commandment?

entries.body: The fifth commandment requires the preserving the honor, and performing the duties belonging to every one in their several places and relations, as superiors, inferiors, or equals.
entries.prompt: What is required in the fifth commandment?

entries.body: The fifth commandment forbids the neglecting of, or doing anything against the honor and duty which belongs to every one in their several places and relations.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the fifth commandment?

entries.body: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment is, a promise of long life and prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God's glory and their own good) to all such as keep this commandment.
entries.prompt: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment?

entries.body: The sixth commandment is, [You shall not kill.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the sixth commandment?

entries.body: The sixth commandment requires all lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others.
entries.prompt: What is required in the sixth commandment?

entries.body: The sixth commandment forbids the taking away of our own life, or the life of our neighbor unjustly, or whatever tends thereunto.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?

entries.body: The seventh commandment is, [You shall not commit adultery.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the seventh commandment?

entries.body: The seventh commandment requires the preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart, speech, and behavior.
entries.prompt: What is required in the seventh commandment?

entries.body: The seventh commandment forbids all unchaste thoughts, words, and actions.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the seventh commandment?

entries.body: The eighth commandment is, [You shall not steal.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the eighth commandment?

entries.body: The eighth commandment requires the lawful procuring and furthering the wealth, and outward estate of ourselves and others.
entries.prompt: What is required in the eighth commandment?

entries.body: The eighth commandment forbids whatever does, or may unjustly hinder our own, or our neighbor's wealth, or outward estate.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?

entries.body: The ninth commandment is, [You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the ninth commandment?

entries.body: The ninth commandment requires the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own and our neighbor's good name, especially in witness-bearing.
entries.prompt: What is required in the ninth commandment?

entries.body: The ninth commandment forbids whatever is prejudicial to truth, or injurious to our own or our neighbor's good name.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the ninth commandment?

entries.body: The tenth commandment is, [You shall not covet your neighbor's house, you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor's.]
entries.prompt: WHICH is the tenth commandment?

entries.body: The tenth commandment requires full contentment with our own condition, and a right and charitable frame of spirit towards our neighbor, and all that is his.
entries.prompt: What is required in the tenth commandment?

entries.body: The tenth commandment forbids all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbor, and all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.
entries.prompt: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?

entries.body: No mere man since the fail is able in this life perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but does daily break them in thought, word, and deed.
entries.prompt: IS any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?

entries.body: Some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.
entries.prompt: ARE all transgressions of the law equally heinous?

entries.body: Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse, both in this life and in that which is to come.
entries.prompt: WHAT does every sin deserve?

entries.body: To escape the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin, God requires of us faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, with the diligent use of all the outward means, whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption.
entries.prompt: WHAT does God require of us, that we may escape his wrath and curse due to us for sin?

entries.body: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is offered to us in the gospel.
entries.prompt: WHAT is faith in Jesus Christ?

entries.body: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sin, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, does with grief and hatred of his sin, turn from it unto God, with full purpose of, and endeavor after new obedience.
entries.prompt: WHAT is repentance unto life?

entries.body: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption, are his ordinances; especially the word, sacraments, and prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for salvation.
entries.prompt: WHAT are the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption?

entries.body: The Spirit of God makes the reading, but especially the preaching of the word, an effectual means of convincing and converting sinners; and building them up in holiness and comfort, through faith, unto salvation.
entries.prompt: HOW is the word made effectual to salvation?

entries.body: That the word may become effectual to salvation, we must attend thereunto with diligence, preparation, and prayer, receive it with faith and love, lay it up in your hearts, and practice it in your lives.
entries.prompt: HOW is the word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to salvation?

entries.body: The sacraments become effectual means of salvation, not from any virtue in them, or in him that does administer them, but only by the blessing of Christ, and the working of his Spirit in them that by faith receive them.
entries.prompt: HOW do the sacraments become effectual means of salvation?

entries.body: A sacrament is a holy ordinance instituted by Christ; wherein by sensible signs, Christ and the benefits of the new covenant are represented, sealed, and applied to believers.
entries.prompt: WHAT is a sacrament?

entries.body: The sacraments of the New Testament are, baptism and the Lord's supper.
entries.prompt: WHICH are the sacraments of the New Testament?

entries.body: Baptism is a sacrament, wherein the washing with water, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, does signify and seal our ingrafting into Christ, and partaking of the benefits of the covenant of grace, and our engagement to be the Lord's.
entries.prompt: WHAT is baptism?

entries.body: Baptism is not to be administered to any that are out of the visible church, until they profess their faith in Christ, and obedience to him; but the infants of such as are members of the visible church are to be baptized.
entries.prompt: TO whom is baptism to be administered?

entries.body: The Lord's supper is a sacrament, wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine, according to Christ's appointment, his death is showed forth; and the worthy receivers are not after a corporal and carnal manner, but by faith made partakers of his body and blood, with all his benefits, to their spiritual nourishment, and growth in grace.
entries.prompt: WHAT is the Lord's supper?

entries.body: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord's supper, that they examine themselves of their knowledge to discern the Lord's body; of their faith to feed upon him; of their repentance, love, and new obedience; lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink judgment to themselves.
entries.prompt: WHAT is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?

entries.body: Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, for things agreeable to his will, in the name of Christ, with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.
entries.prompt: WHAT is prayer?

entries.body: The whole word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but the special rule of direction, is that form of prayer which Christ taught his disciples, commonly called the Lord's prayer.
entries.prompt: WHAT rule has God given for our direction in the duty of prayer?

entries.body: The preface to the Lord's prayer, which is, [Our Father which are in Heaven,] teaches us to draw near to God with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a Father, able and ready to help us: and that we should pray with and for others.
entries.prompt: WHAT does the preface of the Lord's prayer teach us?

entries.body: In the first petition, which is, [Hallowed be your name,] we pray, that God would enable us and others, to glorify him in all that whereby he makes himself known, and that he would dispose all things to his own glory.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the first petition?

entries.body: In the second petition, which is, [Your kingdom come,] we pray that Satan's kingdom may be destroyed, and that the kingdom of grace may be advanced, ourselves and others brought into it, and kept in it, and that the kingdom of glory may be hastened.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the second petition?

entries.body: In the third petition, which is, [Your will be done in earth as it is in Heaven], we pray that God, by his grace, would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his will in all things, as the angels do in Heaven.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the third petition?

entries.body: In the fourth petition, which is, [Give us this day our daily bread,] we pray that of God's free gift we may receive a competent portion of the good things of this life, and enjoy his blessing with them.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the fourth petition?

entries.body: In the fifth petition, which is, [And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,] we pray, that God, for Chris's sake, would freely pardon all our sins; which we are the rather encouraged to ask, because by his grace we are enabled from the heart to forgive others.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the fifth petition?

entries.body: In the sixth petition, which is, [And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil:] we pray, that God would either keep us from being tempted to sin, or support and deliver us when we are tempted.
entries.prompt: WHAT do we pray for in the sixth petition?

entries.body: The conclusion of the Lord's prayer, which is, [For your is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever and ever; Amen.] teaches us, to take our encouragement in prayer from God only; and in our prayers to praise him; ascribing kingdom, power, and glory to him; and in testimony of our desire, and assurance, to be heard, we say, Amen.
entries.prompt: WHAT does the conclusion of the Lord's prayer teach us?
